page: Amazon Web Services m8i.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. It features 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It has a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with read-only and write large-block tests reaching top-tier status. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average and strong categories respectively. Additionally, while LLM prompt processing is strong, text generation speeds for small models are poor, representing a clear performance tradeoff for sequential generation tasks.

Given its bare-metal architecture and massive resource density, the m8i.metal-96xl offers high qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that can leverage its 384 vCPUs and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. It is highly suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, Redis deployments, and software compilation. It is less optimal for workloads requiring local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration.
